title: Accessing data from the PLAZA database
text: PLAZA (Van Bel et al. 2022) database plant comparative functional genomics, centralizing data produced different genome sequencing initiatives. Like Ensembl (Dyer et al. 2025), PLAZA organizes data instances based clades (green) tree life (PLAZA Dicots, PLAZA Monocots, PLAZA Diatoms, pico-PLAZA). Besides rich web server users can interactively search explore plant genomic data, PLAZA offers bulk download data, including whole-genome locus sequences, gene annotations, functional annotations, homology, etc. rplaza provides R interface PLAZA database, allowing direct import PLAZA data R session using standard R/Bioconductor classes, allowing seamless interoperability integration Bioconductor packages. Data types provided PLAZA stored interoperability R/Bioconductor packages summarized :

title: Accessing data from the PLAZA database
text: PLAZA database divided four instances specialized different clades: PLAZA Dicots: focus eudicot plants (N = 98 species); PLAZA Monocots: focus monocot plants (N = 52 species); pico-PLAZA: focus eukaryotic micro-organisms (N = 39 species); PLAZA Diatoms: focus diatoms (N = 26 species). access data species can found instance, well associated metadata (taxonomic information, data sources, etc), can inspect object plaza_metadata, comes rplaza. object list data frames, one PLAZA instance. can see, list four data frames. want look species PLAZA Dicots, instance, need extract corresponding data frame list. Note PLAZA gives unique IDs species, available column PLAZA_ID data frame. PLAZA species IDs essential work rplaza, functions package require specifying species using PLAZA IDs. also important keep mind species present multiple PLAZA instances (e.g., Arabidopsis thaliana), ’re combining data frames single data frame, need remove duplicate rows. example: combining data frames together removing duplicates, can see 171 unique species across PLAZA instances.
